title: How a Chatbot Reads Your Docs Before It Answers
subtitle: RAG gives your docs a librarian, a memory, and a local brain
intro: You ask your docs chatbot a question and it answers like it actually read everything. It didn't memorize it — it looked it up first.
takeaway: RAG lets a chatbot retrieve your docs first, then generate an answer from them.

sections.heading: Everyday analogy: the librarian with sticky notes
sections.body: Imagine a librarian who doesn't memorize books. She puts a sticky note on every paragraph about what it means. When you ask a question, she matches it to the best notes, pulls those pages, and gives them to a writer to answer. That's RAG — Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Retrieval means finding pages first. Generation means writing the answer from them.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? Don't just trust the AI's memory
sections.body: A language model alone doesn't know your MkDocs docs. Obelisk fixes that. First it chunks your docs. Then Ollama creates vector embeddings — number lists that capture meaning. These go into ChromaDB — a vector storage you can search by meaning, not just keywords. At ask time, it retrieves the closest chunks and sends them plus your question to the language model to write a grounded answer. It also offers an OpenAI-compatible API.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? Wrong notes, stale pages
sections.body: If embeddings are poor, retrieval pulls wrong paragraphs and the answer sounds confident but wrong. If docs change and indexing lags, it answers from old pages. Obelisk watches files and re-indexes them quickly. Running local models with Ollama also needs enough computer power and Docker setup, or answers get slow. Always check: did it retrieve the right source first?

steps.narration: Start with your MkDocs docs — the knowledge you want searchable.
Ollama turns each chunk into a vector embedding, a meaning sticky note.
ChromaDB stores those vectors so you can search by meaning.
You ask a question in plain language.
The system retrieves the most similar chunks.
The LLM generates an answer using your question plus retrieved context.

quiz.q: What does Retrieval-Augmented Generation mainly do?
options: It finds your docs first, then writes an answer from them
It trains a new LLM from scratch
It only checks spelling in docs
quiz.why: RAG = retrieval step to find relevant docs, then generation step to answer using them as context.

quiz.q: What fails first if you have 100x more docs and bad embeddings?
options: Retrieval pulls wrong pages and answers become wrong
quiz.why: With more docs, poor embeddings cause mismatched search — the LLM then generates from wrong context.

quiz.q: Why does Obelisk use Ollama and ChromaDB?
options: Ollama creates meaning vectors and generates locally; ChromaDB stores and searches them
They are needed to write Markdown
They replace the need for any docs
quiz.why: Obelisk uses Ollama for local embeddings and generation, and ChromaDB as vector storage for semantic search.
